material_findings.primary_facts: The simple protocol can lose edits; guaranteed delivery changes retained state. Failed patches can be reversed out, beyond misplacement.
material_findings.consequence: These distinctions affect the assigned offline failure boundary and history tradeoff. The report neither identifies the variant nor preserves this consequential uncertainty. No deployment or guaranteed-delivery implementation is demanded.

material_findings.summary: A particular in-flight discard exchange is generalized into an inherent merge-based synchronization limit.

sections: §1 Conventional Strategies, three-step server exchange and changes-during-flight condition

material_findings.primary_facts: Fraser scopes that limit to an exchange that discards received text if local editing occurs during flight. GNU merge operates on supplied versions.
material_findings.consequence: The bounded alternative is merge on reconnect. Making this conditional exchange behavior its categorical characteristic failure can wrongly discount a legitimate alternative.
material_findings.disposition: Unsupported consequential scope extension; prevents PASS/PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS.

limitations.assessment: Yjs metadata growth is a legitimate unresolved concern, but implementation GC/struct merging and the distinction between convergence and durable edit-history preservation are absent. The claimed absolute smallness cannot follow from a 20 KB current-text bound. Do not read this as a measured byte guarantee.

Generic event-passing loss warnings are accurate in their original context. The ShareDB implementation contains recovery/retry/version handling. Permanent op loss is different from an ordinary disconnected or dropped-message episode. The candidate does not specify the loss class; this caveat is not used as an independently decisive failure.

Conflict/overlap and escalation depend on merge granularity/options and product policy. Do not allege that GNU default -m necessarily accepts identical concurrent changes: it defaults to -A; -e/-E treat matching tips differently. No exact diff3 invocation was proposed or executed.
The edition/date historical lead is sufficient. Copyright lineage is not evidence for every semantic rule remaining unchanged for decades.
